output.brief: The gateway 5.8 release is not the cause. The regression began in each cell within minutes of the storage compaction tuning push (FC-7710) on the evening of 2 Nov. That push tripled compaction threads, which drove disk use from 41% to 97% and node-side GET time from 61 ms to 262 ms. Cell aps-3 skipped the push and got 5.8 anyway, and its p99 stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. The network does not explain it either. Do not roll back the gateway. That would not fix latency and would reopen the security hole, which has a 30 Nov audit deadline. Do not pause compaction. The backlog would grow toward the 15% level, where reads get worse and nodes risk filling their disks. Next, revert FC-7710 in one cell, for example a cell like use-1, and watch GET p99 and backlog. If p99 recovers, extend the revert to the rest. Keep watching backlog, since the revert drops compaction back to 2 threads. Hold off on throttling Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution job shows where the backlog came from. The expiry sweep is another candidate. Profiling the gateway's CPU increase is low priority. I'm quite confident in this, though the Orrin link is still unproven.
